papers.title: On Subquadratic Architectures: From Applications to Principles
papers.abstract: Transformers have quadratic attention costs. This work compares xLSTM, Mamba-2, and Gated DeltaNet on code-model pretraining, distillation, and time-series tasks. xLSTM delivers strongest performance through superior state tracking and memory dynamics via its gating scheme.

papers.title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
papers.abstract: Grammar-constrained decoding ensures syntactic validity but can be exploited as attack surface. CodeSpear jailbreaks LLMs through benign grammar constraints. CodeShield aligns models in code modality using honeypot code to restore safety without sacrificing utility.

papers.title: TRACE: A Unified Rollout Budget Allocation Framework for Efficient Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards suffers from insufficient reward contrast in multi-turn rollouts. TRACE extends budget allocation from prompt roots to turn-level prefixes, forming tree-structured rollouts that amplify policy-update signals and improve task performance.

papers.title: Reroute, Don't Remove: Recoverable Visual Token Routing for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models project images into hundreds to thousands of visual tokens, making decoder inference expensive. Existing methods follow rank-and-remove paradigms, but token importance changes across decoder depth. Reroute replaces removal with recoverable routing, allowing deferred tokens to re-enter at later stages.

papers.title: Breaking the Bubble: Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel Training with Bounded Weight Inconsistency
papers.abstract: Pipeline parallelism trades throughput, memory, and optimization consistency. PACI enables bubble-free asynchronous training by bounding forward/backward version drift through local gradient accumulation, improving training time-to-accuracy by 1.69× without sacrificing stability.

papers.title: ReVision: Scaling Computer-Use Agents via Temporal Visual Redundancy Reduction
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents encode screenshots into many visual tokens, limiting trajectory history under fixed budgets. ReVision removes redundant visual patches across consecutive frames while preserving spatial structure, reducing token usage by 46% and improving success rates.

papers.title: DRIFT: A Residual Flow Adapter for Decoding Continuous Outputs in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models using discrete tokens suit text but not continuous outputs like temporal boundaries or robotic control. DRIFT combines base predictor with flow-matching refinement, transforming prediction from global to localized residual distributions for improved generalization.

papers.title: Fine-tuning Multi-modal LLMs with ART: Art-based Reinforcement Training
papers.abstract: LoRA and soft prompting both require modifying computational graphs of precompiled LLMs. ART injects information by optimizing raw visual input on frozen models, supporting any fine-tuning objective while achieving LoRA-competitive accuracy on mathematics and structured-tool-use tasks.

papers.title: Adaptive Multi-Resolution Procedural Knowledge Compression for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Reusable skills injected into LLM applications incur significant prefill costs when repeated. SKIM compresses skills adaptively through soft tokens without requiring explicit human annotations, preserving task performance while reducing token length to 30-60% of original.

papers.title: τ-Rec: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Recommender Systems
papers.abstract: Agentic recommender systems lack evaluation beyond subjective LLM-as-judge methods. τ-Rec replaces subjectivity with verifiable rewards and controlled dialogue constraints. Testing nine model configurations reveals steep reliability cliffs with best models achieving only ~57% at pass^1.

cc_updates.body:
Fixed Fable 5 model names with a `[1m]` suffix not being normalized — Fable 5 includes 1M context by default, so the suffix is now stripped automatically
Fixed a spurious "sandbox dependencies missing" startup warning on Windows when sandbox was enabled in settings

Sub-agents can now spawn their own sub-agents (up to 5 levels deep)
Amazon Bedrock now reads the AWS region from `~/.aws` config files when `AWS_REGION` isn't set, matching AWS SDK precedence; `/status` shows where the region came from
Added a search bar when browsing a marketplace's plugins in `/plugin`
Added `model` attribute to the `claude_code.lines_of_code.count` OTEL metric
Fixed sessions using 1M context without usage credits getting permanently stuck — the session now automatically compacts back under the standard context limit
Fixed a repeating "an image in the conversation could not be processed and was removed" error
Fixed the agents view keeping a session under Working with a busy spinner for up to 30 seconds after the worker replied
Fixed background agents potentially reading another directory's project settings when dispatched onto a pre-warmed worker

Introducing Claude Fable 5: a Mythos-class model that we've made safe for general use. Fable's capabilities exceed those of any model we've ever made generally available. Update to version 2.1.170 for access.
Fixed sessions not saving transcripts (and not appearing in --resume) when launched from the VS Code integrated terminal or any shell that inherited Claude Code environment variables.
